figure:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: transparent photographic stop-motion sprite atlas for the existing Sonar landing hero.
Input image 1 is the edit target and exact character / clothing / prop reference. Preserve this same adult woman, slick dark hair, coral cat-eye sunglasses, gold hoop earrings, black outfit, cream newspaper and editorial lighting.
Create ONE high-resolution PNG atlas with exactly 12 separate full cutout frames in a perfectly regular 4-column by 3-row grid, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Canvas ideally 3072x3072 pixels. Each of the 12 equal square cells contains the SAME woman from top of hair to hips, centered at the same position and scale. Keep the whole person and whole paper within each cell with generous transparent margins on all sides, consistent head height and waist baseline. No labels, no panel borders. True transparent alpha background, no checkerboard drawn in, no floor or shadows outside the cutout.
This is a subtle photographic stop-motion sequence, with actual arm, hand, paper and head poses, NOT twelve identical stills. Paper opens at a vertical center fold like a broadsheet. All anatomy natural, two hands gripping outer edges.
Frame 1: holding the newspaper vertically half folded in front of torso, reading it, chin slightly down.
Frame 2: begin unfolding, hands moving outward, paper about 55% open.
Frame 3: newspaper 75% open, chin lifting.
Frame 4: newspaper almost fully open, head level.
Frame 5: newspaper fully open matching reference, calmly looking forward.
Frame 6: fully open paper, eyes/head begin to turn toward her RIGHT (viewer LEFT) where a camera is.
Frame 7: a small surprised recoil to a camera flash, chin up, shoulders raised just a little, mouth slightly parted, paper dips 2 cm. Do NOT draw light, glow or camera.
Frame 8: warm restrained smile toward viewer LEFT, chin tilted 5 degrees, newspaper open.
Frame 9: relaxed smile looking forward again, newspaper open.
Frame 10: looking slightly down and toward viewer RIGHT with a curious smile, paper still open.
Frame 11: begin folding the paper inward again, about 75% open.
Frame 12: newspaper about 55% open, returning to the initial pose.
Keep poses close enough for an animation: no big leaps, no changing character identity, camera angle, hairstyle, accessories, outfit or paper design between cells. The newspaper must remain cream with black serif headlines. Preserve the reference's readable text consistently when visible: "THE SONAR REPORT"; "YOUR MARKET, ON CAMERA"; "The competitors in your niche"; "The creators posting for them"; "The clips that broke out"; "Every number cited. Every video linked."; "HEAR WHAT YOUR MARKET IS SAYING". Folds naturally hide some text. Preserve clear hands and fingers. No extra objects, no extra people in a cell, no background, no watermark. Crisp photographic details.
camera:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: photographic stop-motion sprite atlas with TRUE transparent background.
Image 1 is the exact edit target: preserve the same black mirrorless camera, same large lens pointing toward viewer RIGHT, same skin tone and hand entering from the LEFT, same lighting and photographic finish.
Make ONE 3-column by 2-row regular sprite atlas containing exactly SIX frames of a single camera shutter-click action. Same camera size, same lens position and same wrist endpoint across all cells, plenty of transparent padding, no contact between cells. High resolution crisp cutouts, no background, no panel borders, no labels, no watermark.
In every cell the hand and wrist enter from the left holding the camera downward exactly as in the reference; the forearm is cropped at the left edge of its image area. No shoulder or body. Keep one anatomically correct hand with five fingers. The movement is deliberately small and coherent, suited to stop-motion.
Frame 1: reference rest pose, shutter finger lifted a little above shutter.
Frame 2: index finger curling toward the shutter, camera tilted upward about two degrees.
Frame 3: index finger presses the shutter fully, camera held firmly.
Frame 4: shutter fully down, tiny natural recoil rotates camera downward about two degrees. No flash drawn into the photo.
Frame 5: finger lifting back up, camera eases back.
Frame 6: rest pose again identical to frame 1.
Preserve camera geometry and lens circularity; do not switch cameras, mirror the shot, show the back of the camera, or draw separate floating fingers. No light effects or glowing lens; those are added separately in the animation.
cameraAlphaPass: Edit this sprite atlas. Remove the ENTIRE background from every pixel outside the six hand-and-camera cutouts. Remove all brown, tan, gray, black mist, shadows, haze and gradients surrounding the six objects. The output must have clean TRUE ALPHA transparency between the hands and cameras and all the way to the edges, like six stickers on an invisible canvas. Keep the exact six camera-and-hand poses, their exact positions, colors, scales and 3-column 2-row layout unchanged. Preserve the camera itself, fingers, hand and forearm only. Do not add a backdrop or checkerboard. No new objects.
headphones:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: photographic stop-motion sprite atlas, TRUE alpha transparent background.
Image 1 is the exact edit target. Preserve the same coral/salmon and cream over-ear headphones, same right-side hand holding the crown of the headband, same skin tone, same lighting. Hand and arm extend from viewer RIGHT. The headphones hang to the left of the hand. Do not mirror.
Make ONE regular 3-column by 2-row atlas with exactly SIX separate frames, ample clear transparent space between each frame. Each cell has one complete hand-and-headphones cutout, never touching the next cell. Same scale and grip-point location in each cell; all of headphones visible. The wrist/arm crops at the right edge of each subject area. No background, no labels, no grid lines, no music icons, no glow, no watermark.
A playful small swinging motion with secondary articulation at the earcup hinges:
1. relaxed reference pose, headphones hanging straight.
2. hand lifts slightly, headband angles 5 degrees toward viewer left, left earcup swings outward slightly.
3. gentle swing left about 9 degrees, earcups turn subtly on hinges, band stays physically connected to both.
4. swings past center toward viewer right 7 degrees, earcups follow.
5. smaller swing left 3 degrees, returns to facing forward.
6. original relaxed pose again matching frame 1.
Crisp photographic editorial realism. Only one hand per cell, five natural fingers, same headphones construction and color, no changing earcup size. Keep arm movement subtle and same grip position so these frames can animate. Preserve true alpha transparency outside each cutout.
